title: Session-priority token-bucket gating + progressive KV-lite degrade strategy for cross-region state stores
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant/session-priority gating layer that integrates token-bucket admission with connection trimming and a progressive 'KV-lite' degrade mode for stateful downstreams (Redis/KV, Kafka, primary DBs). The gating layer should keep high-priority traffic within p99 latency SLOs during regional surge or partial dependency failure by dynamically trimming lower-priority sessions, offloading to stale/approximate responses, and activating region-aware failover. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, tests, dashboarding, and runbook.

Motivation: Recent incidents show tail-latency from state stores causes system-wide cascading queuing (connection saturation -> retries -> amplification). We need a predictable way to contain impact while preserving useful behavior for low-priority workloads instead of hard failures. In contrast to pure circuit-breakers, this approach combines admission control, prioritized graceful degradation, and probabilistic approximate reads to preserve availability and bounded latency.

Scope:
- Admission gating: per-session token-bucket with tenant priority weights and global smoothing window; tokens consumed per request type (write/read/long-poll).
- Connection trimming API: when admission indicates congestion, proactively reduce pool concurrency for low-priority sessions and shift to pipelined/lightweight clients.
- KV-lite degrade mode (Redis/KV): return compact snapshot or probabilistic sketch (Bloom/GCS) + best-effort stale value when fresh value can't meet latency SLO. Provide consistency metadata in payload.
- Kafka degrade mode: for consumer-facing read paths, allow fast fallback to head-offset summaries for lagging partitions and opportunistic hedging to another regional replica when offsets are available.
- DB degrade mode: read-only stale-replica reads with TTL-based staleness and selective index-rewrite to avoid expensive OLTP paths.
- Multi-region failover: warm-standby cache prefetch and region-score based circuit with hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Observability: SLO dashboards, token-bucket utilization, degradation mode activations, per-tenant error/latency curves.
- Runbooks and chaos tests (simulated store latency, partial region outage).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published in Confluence with sequence diagrams, admission API contract, and degradation payload format (includes staleness metadata)
Prototype library implemented server-side that exposes per-session token-bucket admission hooks and connection trimming signals (API + SDK usage example)
KV-lite degrade response format implemented for Redis-backed route and end-to-end unit tests validating staleness metadata and p99 latency improvement under injected tail latency
Canary rollout plan with canary metrics and automatic rollback condition (p99 > 2x baseline for high-priority tenants)
Observability: dashboard with token consumption, degrade-mode activations, per-tenant SLO burn rate, and alert rules created
Runbook and on-call playbook added to SRE with clear remediation steps and circuit-state introspection commands
Chaos test harness (k8s fault injection) reproducibly demonstrates p99 containment for high-priority sessions during simulated Redis/KV 500ms tail latency
implementation_notes: Admission model: each session receives N tokens per second scaled by tenant priority multiplier; writes cost 2 tokens, reads cost 1; long-poll subscriptions cost 0.25 tokens/s while active

Global oversubscription guard: global token pool that prevents aggregate bursting across many small tenants; when exhausted, score-based trimming chooses victim sessions (lowest priority, lowest recent success rate)
Connection trimming: expose pool.SlimDown(lowWaterMark) hook which scales down per-connection concurrency; clients will be updated to accept pipelined single-connection mode for low-priority sessions

KV-lite design: store maintains lightweight persistent snapshot cache (compact LSN + compressed key subset). On degrade, API returns {value, staleness_ms, mode: 'kv-lite', confidence_score}. Accepts client opt-in header to allow approximate results.

Kafka fallback: if consumer partition latency > threshold, return 'offset-summary' with truncated message payloads + metadata and schedule asynchronous hedged-fetch to alternate regional replica. Client SDK exposes 'prefer-summary' flag to trade fidelity for latency
DB degrade: preferential routing to read-replicas with bounded staleness value; add SQL hint to skip analytical joins and return abbreviated result where safe

Circuit semantics: score-based circuit (0..100) per region+store combining error rates, median latency, and token-saturation. Open circuit when score > 80 for 30s, with exponential backoff and manual override via console
Compatibility: new admission hooks must be backward compatible; default for unknown clients is 'opt-out' meaning they continue to get full fidelity until they adopt headers
Security: ensure staleness/approximate payloads do not leak sensitive fields. Degrade responses must pass PII scrub or follow redaction config
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design & specs) - 1 week: agree on API contract, payload schemas, and priority weighting table (Owners: Marco, Evelyn Chen)
Phase 1 (library + unit tests) - 2 weeks: implement admission library and pool hooks; expose server SDK integration points
Phase 2 (KV-lite prototype) - 2 weeks: implement degrade response for a single Redis-backed route and add E2E latency tests
Phase 3 (canary) - 1 week: enable on 5% traffic for non-critical tenants in us-west with automated rollback triggers
Phase 4 (expand) - 2 weeks: add Kafka & DB degrade modes, multi-region scoring, and observability
Phase 5 (SRE runbook + chaos) - 1 week: add runbook, chaos experiments, and schedule practice drill with on-call
Phase 6 (GA) - after metrics stable: full cluster rollout and postmortem review
monitoring_and_kpis: Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency pre/post degrade activation
Token-bucket refill/utilization rates and global exhaustion events
Degrade-mode activations per region/store and average staleness_ms returned
Error uplift (5xx) and client-side degradation counters
Circuit scores and open/close events (with reason tag)
SLO burn rate alerts for high-priority tenants (email + pager at 3x burn)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Client apps assume strong consistency and may misinterpret stale responses -> Mitigation: opt-in header, explicit staleness metadata, and developer docs explaining semantics
Risk: Attack surface for information leakage via approximate payloads -> Mitigation: require redaction rules applied before degrade responses; add security review gating
Risk: Oscillation between regions causing flapping failover -> Mitigation: hysteresis windows, region-score smoothing, manual override in console
Risk: Complexity increases operational overhead -> Mitigation: start with single route prototype, keep payloads simple, and provide clear runbooks
dependencies: Console: UI for manual circuit override and per-tenant priority weight (PM owner: Lina Gomez)
SDKs: opt-in headers and client flags (Dev exp owner: Ivan Novak)
Security: PII redaction rules and review (owner: Security team)
SRE: chaos test scheduling and alerts (owner: SRE oncall)
Infra: additional replica snapshot store for KV-lite cached snapshots
